tools.name: Qualytics
tools.tagline: Data quality platform that infers checks automatically and lets teams author more checks in a low-code UI.
tools.bestFor: Enterprises that want AI-generated rule coverage plus cross-system data diffs and reconciliation
tools.description: Qualytics profiles tables and files, generates quality checks automatically (AI Managed checks) and lets users add Authored checks from a library of rule types in a form-based UI. Its rule types include Data Diff, which compares a target container with a reference container row by row, including across datastores, plus Is Replica Of and Aggregation Comparison. It runs as a single-tenant managed deployment or self-hosted on Kubernetes, and pricing is not published.
pros: Data Diff check compares two containers row by row and the reference can live in a different datastore
Tests files directly in S3, Azure Data Lake Storage and Google Cloud Storage (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, ORC, Delta, Iceberg, XLSX and more)
Scan schedules: hourly, daily, weekly or a five-field cron expression
Flows send notifications to email, Slack, Microsoft Teams and PagerDuty
30-day free trial set up by the Qualytics team on a portion of your own data
cons: No public pricing; quote only
The CLI runs scans from GitHub Actions, but the docs do not say a failed check fails the build
Managed deployment is single-tenant, and Qualytics provisions it rather than offering self-serve sign-up
Founding year and headquarters are not stated on the website
tools.trial: 30-day free trial: the Qualytics team sets up an environment on a representative portion of your warehouse, lakehouse or pipeline

tools.name: Validio
tools.tagline: Agentic data management platform that combines validators, ML anomaly detection, lineage and a catalog.
tools.bestFor: Enterprises, including regulated ones, that want warehouse and stream validation with a managed or in-VPC deployment
tools.description: Validio runs validators on warehouse tables, streams and custom SQL sources on a polling schedule and raises incidents when metrics cross fixed or dynamic thresholds. Validator types include null, enum, distinct and duplicate values, freshness, custom SQL, referential integrity against a reference source, and a Reconciliation validator that compares metric results across two sources. Pricing is custom and depends on the number of data assets, segments and the deployment model, with a 14-day trial.
pros: Validators are set up in a UI wizard, with AI validator recommendations and text-to-SQL for custom SQL
Reconciliation, Relative Volume and Referential Integrity validators compare data across two sources
Notification channels for Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, webhooks, Jira and ServiceNow
Managed deployment on GCP, AWS or Azure, or self-hosted in your VPC with a Helm chart
Lists ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certification, plus GDPR and HIPAA compliance
cons: No public prices; quote based on data assets, segments and deployment model
Reconciliation compares computed metrics, not individual rows
Object-storage data is reached through Amazon Athena; direct CSV or Parquet file testing is not documented
CI/CD use (GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, Azure DevOps) goes through the API or SDK rather than a packaged action
tools.trial: 14-day trial of the full platform, up to 10 users, with your own data or demo datasets

plans.name: Custom

tools.name: Telmai
tools.tagline: AI-based data observability and validation for data lakes, lakehouses and warehouses.
tools.bestFor: Teams validating data in open lakehouse formats and object storage as well as warehouses
tools.description: Telmai profiles assets from warehouses and cloud storage, runs out-of-the-box and user-defined monitors (built-in metrics, record validation rules and SQL rules), and alerts on incidents. Its Data comparison feature compares an asset with another asset by ID, counts new, missing and changed records, and writes the changed records to a bucket as JSON or Parquet. It runs as SaaS, hybrid (scans on your own Spark) or fully in your VPC, and pricing is by demo request.
pros: Reads CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, Delta Lake and XML files directly from S3, Azure Blob and Google Cloud Storage
Data comparison finds new, missing and changed records between two assets
Four-step monitor builder in the UI, plus AI monitor recommendations
Scheduled scans per asset or in bulk, and alerts to Slack, Microsoft Teams, email or webhooks
Hybrid and VPC deployments keep row-level data in your environment
cons: No public pricing, trial or free plan; demo request only
Circuit breakers need API calls from an orchestrator such as Airflow; no CI/CD integration is documented
Data comparison is not available for assets in a group
Founding year is not stated on the website

tools.name: SYNQ (Coalesce Quality)
tools.tagline: Data observability and testing built around data products, now sold as Coalesce Quality.
tools.bestFor: dbt, SQLMesh and Coalesce teams that want tests, anomaly monitors and cross-database reconciliation in one place
tools.description: SYNQ was acquired by Coalesce, announced on March 10, 2026, and is now Coalesce Quality; synq.io/pricing redirects to Coalesce's pricing, where Quality is included in every plan. It combines SQL tests (not_null, unique, accepted values, relationships, business rules and custom queries) that you can create in the app or in YAML, self-learning anomaly monitors, and a reconciliation CLI (synq-recon) that compares datasets across databases by row counts and checksums. The free Developer plan covers 1 user, and Starter costs $150 per user per month, billed annually.
pros: Reconciliation compares source and target across databases and clouds, and drills down to differing key ranges
synq-recon can act as a CI/CD release gate with --fail-on and documented exit codes
SQL test types (not_null, unique, accepted_values, min_max, relationships and more) work the same in the app, API and YAML
Alerts to Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, PagerDuty and Opsgenie
Free Developer plan (1 user) includes Quality
cons: No longer a standalone vendor: pricing and plans are Coalesce's, and Coalesce describes Quality as built into its platform
Starter is $150 per user per month on annual billing only, with no monthly price shown
SaaS only, hosted on Google Cloud in the EU, US and AU regions; an on-premise agent covers database access only
Direct file testing (CSV, Parquet) is not documented

tools.name: Reladiff
tools.tagline: Open-source CLI and Python library for diffing large tables within or across databases.
tools.bestFor: Engineers checking that a migrated or replicated table matches its source, from the command line or Python
tools.description: Reladiff is an MIT-licensed fork of Datafold's archived data-diff project. It diffs tables across databases (for example PostgreSQL to Snowflake) with a hash-based divide-and-conquer algorithm, or within one database with a join, and outputs git-style or JSON diffs. Version 0.6.0 was released on PyPI on 2025-03-04.
pros: Free and open source (MIT)
Cross-database diffs with only the changed segments downloaded; the README cites over 1B rows in about 5 minutes when there are no differences
Supports more than a dozen databases, including Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, DuckDB and Trino
JSON output and a Python API for automation
cons: Diffing only: no rule checks, scheduling, alerts or UI are documented
BigQuery and Databricks support is marked 'implemented, with limited testing'
Small project: last release v0.6.0 in March 2025 and last commit in August 2025
The docs do not describe an exit code that fails a CI build when differences are found
tools.freePlanDetails: Open-source CLI and Python library (MIT), installed with pip
